Teaching

Teaching, learning, and occasional debugging

A collection of topics, course materials, and useful resources for students.

01

Object-Oriented Programming

Bachelor, 1st year, summer semester

Teaching core OOP principles such as classes, encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, constructors, exceptions, and practical C++ programming.

Workshop materials
02

Databases

Bachelor, 2nd year, summer semester

Introduction to relational database systems, including data modeling, ER diagrams, SQL, normalization, database design, and practical work with relational databases.

03

Course Project

Bachelor, 3rd year, summer semester

A project-based course where students work under the supervision of a chosen faculty member to design and develop a semester-long project. The course emphasizes practical problem-solving, independent work, research, software or system development, and project presentation.

04

Information Systems

Bachelor, 4th year, winter semester

Courses focused on the analysis, design, and development of information systems, including process modeling, data modeling, and practical implementation.

05

Computer Vision

Bachelor, 4th year, summer semester

Topics include image processing, geometric transformations, filtering, edge detection, and practical work with Python and OpenCV.

06

Advanced Databases

Masters, 1st year, winter semester

Explores advanced database concepts including optimization, transactions, distributed databases, and modern NoSQL approaches such as document, key-value, and graph databases, with practical applications.

07

Introduction to IoT

Masters, 1st year, summer semester

Covers the fundamentals of the Internet of Things, including sensors, microcontrollers, communication protocols, data collection, IoT architectures, and introductory hands-on work with connected devices and smart systems.

Student supervision

Supervised Bachelor’s and Master’s Graduates

Teaching, mentoring, and supervising — because one project somehow became many. A collection of bachelor’s and master’s student projects, built through curiosity, experimentation, and persistence.
